To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RFBs using Fe(DIPSO)/Fe(CN) 6 as redox couple have a great potential as a promising energy storage system for stationary applications.
Fe(DIP SO) and ferrocyanides are the promising active species for RFB and the Fe(DIP SO), which has strong resistance against the conversion to Fe(s), is the best negative active species for RFP.

a novel organometallic material consisting of iron and DIPSO ligand is newly suggested as a negative active species for RFB and when it is used together with the conventional positive active species of ferrocyanide, it shows high power and energy density as well as excellent cycle stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new iron based aqueous organometallic complex for the application of RFB.
the RFB using the organometallic complex as negative active species.
a novel RFB that is composed of organometallic complex and redox couple.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fe(DIPOS) has a strong potential to replace the Fe(TEA).
Fe(DIPSA) is a very promising negative active material for RFB.
the Fe(DIP SO) is a promising candidate for negative active species for iron aqueous red ox flow batteries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RFBs using organometal complex consisting of iron with 3 [bis(2-hydroxyethyl)amio] 2 hydroxyl propanesulfonic ligand and ferrocyamide as redox couple have the advantages of high energy density, high power density, long cycle life and high coulombic efficiency and this can be applied to large scale energy storage systems.
Fe(DIPSA) is a new organometallic complex that is very promising as negative active species of iron based aqueous redox RFB.
a RFB using Fe(DIPSO)/Fe(CN) redox couple can be considered as a promising alternative for the next generation RFBs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RFB with the Fe(DIPOS) and Fe(Cn)6 can be a promising candidate for large scale energy storage applications due to its high energy efficiency and excellent cycle performance.
Fe(DIPSA) is a promising candidate for negative active species of RFBs.
the RFB based on the Fe(DIPOS)/Fe(CN) redox couple is promising for the large scale application of RFB.
